WHAT IT DOES: (a) access_requests_pin_scope_ck and consent_grants_pin_scope_ck (0033) allow read_records or write_records for a patient_access_pin row (still direct-care, never break-glass), dropped and added NOT VALID then validated; (b) CREATE OR REPLACE identity.access_patient_with_pin(text,text,integer) from 0098's body (md5 830c1baa4bca3df57cc02b7b002a8831 before, e17925c512f5f3e9fc79d84faded6ea1 after): every grant lasts exactly 1440 minutes whatever is asked (5-1440 still checked), request and grant are write_records, only a still-valid write_records PIN grant is reused, a deny of reading or writing (or every action) stops it, and the audit details and PatientAccessPinVerified payload carry scope; signature, result, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and ACL unchanged and compared after; (c) identity_outbox_minimum_necessary accepts the PIN notice with or without scope; (d) ALTER POLICY identity_outbox_patient_access_pin_insert admits a PIN grant of either scope and a payload scope equal to the grant's. No table, column, index, trigger, role, permission or grant change; runtime-grants.sql unchanged (sha256 0da043d1f2ccba7e3c17af09772bea2da6f9d091e2986c9144a6c999d52fe9bf, production's), so it is not declared; no row written. 0109-0121 change none of the objects 0122 reads or replaces (their md5 pins hold on 0001-0121). The new identity-api in this branch defaults to 1440 and accepts 5-1440. The event dispatcher and notification worker already accept the three-key PIN notice (hid-system#206, live since 2026-11-11). apps/web (#207) asks 1440 and says 'see and add to records for 24 hours'.
